name: browser-use
headline: Open Ralph Wiggum - AI Coding Loops
short_description: Open Ralph Wiggum enables developers to run iterative AI coding loops with Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. Type 'ralph "prompt"' to start or use a prompt file. Check status and automate repetitive coding tasks.
author: Th0rgal

sections.overview:
Open Ralph Wiggum is a tool that enables developers to execute iterative AI coding loops integrated with Claude Code and Cursor Agent. Users can start the automation by typing 'ralph "prompt"' or using a prompt file, which triggers multi-step coding iterations. The skill handles stream-based output from Claude Code with support for partial messages and JSON formatting. It automates repetitive coding tasks by managing the feedback loop between prompts and AI-generated code, reducing manual intervention. Developers benefit from faster code generation and testing cycles without needing to manually manage each iteration.
Automate the creation of a REST API with CRUD operations and tests.
Iteratively develop a CLI tool while monitoring progress.
Manage complex projects by breaking them into smaller tasks with structured tracking.
Run self-correcting loops for code refactoring and bug fixing.
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/Th0rgal/open-ralph-wiggum`
sections.usage:
```
Use open-ralph-wiggum to automate the following iterative coding task: [DESCRIBE_TASK]. Start by running 'ralph "[INITIAL_PROMPT]"' to initiate the loop. Monitor progress with 'ralph status' and iterate until the task is complete. Example: 'ralph "Refactor the user authentication module in /src/auth to use JWT tokens instead of sessions. Start by analyzing the current codebase."'
```
Copy

```
```bash
$ ralph "Refactor the user authentication module in /src/auth to use JWT tokens instead of sessions. Start by analyzing the current codebase."

Ralph Wiggum v1.2.0 | Iteration 1/5
Analyzing /src/auth... Found 12 files using session-based auth.

Suggested changes:
1. Replace session middleware with JWT in /src/auth/middleware.js
2. Update /src/auth/models/User.js to store refresh tokens
3. Modify /src/auth/routes/login.js to issue JWT tokens

Applying changes to /src/auth/middleware.js...
✅ Successfully replaced session middleware with JWT
✅ Updated 4 functions to handle token validation

Ralph Wiggum v1.2.0 | Iteration 2/5
Verifying changes...
⚠️ Warning: /src/auth/routes/logout.js still uses session.destroy()
Suggested fix: Replace with token invalidation

Applying changes to /src/auth/routes/logout.js...
✅ Updated logout route to invalidate JWT tokens

Ralph Wiggum v1.2.0 | Iteration 3/5
Running tests...
✅ All 18 auth tests passing (2 new JWT-specific tests added)
✅ Code coverage: 92% (up from 85%)

Ralph Wiggum v1.2.0 | Iteration 4/5
Checking security implications...
✅ No hardcoded secrets found in JWT implementation
✅ Token expiration set to 15 minutes (refresh token: 7 days)

Ralph Wiggum v1.2.0 | Iteration 5/5
Final review complete. Changes ready for PR.

Summary of changes:
- 12 files modified
- 4 new test cases added
- Security vulnerabilities addressed
- Performance improved by 12% (reduced session storage overhead)

Next steps:
1. Review changes in /src/auth/
2. Run 'npm test' locally
3. Create PR with title 'feat(auth): migrate to JWT-based authentication'
```
```
requirements: Claude Code or compatible AI agent
